title: fix(pm): post-stamped REFUSES an artefact whose only stamp token sits inside a quoted span
body:
Fixes #19091

Clause-②: no

`scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs` leaves a `{{NOW}}` inside a Markdown code span verbatim by design, so the tool's own prose can quote the contract. Nothing checked that the artefact ended up **stamped at all**, so a body whose ONLY token was quoted posted at **exit 0** carrying the literal token and no time — the quiet direction the `UNKNOWN` refusal exists to close, reached through the carve-out by spelling the token *correctly*.

## Measured on `main` before the change (dry run, this act, `--repo=objectstack-ai/objectstack`)

| body | exit | status line |
|:---|:---|:---|
| LEG A — stamp only inside a code span | **0** | `0 {{NOW}}, 0 quoted · verbatim: 1 opener(s) …` ⇒ token literal, artefact UNSTAMPED |
| LEG B — same body, stamp in prose | 0 | `1 {{NOW}}, 0 quoted · verbatim: 0 opener(s) …` ⇒ substituted |

## 1. The predicate first

`stampVerdict({ substituted, quoted, verbatimTokens })` — a pure exported function over the counts the render already produces, with `STAMP_VERDICTS` as its declared vocabulary and `REFUSED_STAMP_VERDICT` naming the one that must not reach the board.

| verdict | counts | outcome |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `stamped-by-this-act` | `substituted ≥ 1` | accepted, exit 0 — unchanged |
| `stamped-by-declaration` | `substituted = 0`, `quoted ≥ 1` | **accepted**, exit 0 — a `{{WAS:…}}` rendered from its own declaration IS a stamp |
| `unstamped-quoted-token` | `substituted = 0`, `quoted = 0`, `verbatimTokens ≥ 1` | **REFUSED**, `EXIT_REFUSED` (2), nothing written |
| `no-token` | all three zero | accepted, exit 0 — unchanged |

⛔ The criterion the card excluded is excluded, and pinned as excluded: `stampVerdict({ substituted: 0, quoted: 1, verbatimTokens: 1 })` is `stamped-by-declaration`, not the refusal. That is the tool's own docblock shape — a body that quotes both tokens and stamps itself by declaration.

**`no-token` is deliberately not named by the new refusal.** The reason is a population rather than a preference: every filed instance CARRIED a token, quoted, so the defect is the contradiction between what the body says and what happened, and a body that never spells a token states nothing to contradict. #17314's standing rule binds a timestamp a seat WRITES; a body that writes none breaks it nowhere. Refusing it would be a new required refusal over the whole population of untokened bodies — the older, separately measured shape the card sets aside.

**The count the predicate reads is not the status line's `verbatim`.** `verbatim` counts every opener left as written; `verbatimTokens` counts only the openers that ARE `{{NOW}}` or `{{WAS:…}}`. Measured: a body quoting a fenced `{{ user.name }}` template and stamping nothing reads `verbatim: 1, verbatimTokens: 0` and still posts — refusing it would be a refusal naming a token the body does not carry. That measurement is why the two are two fields, and it is the one place this diff departs from the suggested route's `verbatimOpeners` field name.

## 2. Then the consequence — REFUSED, not warned

The card allowed a loud warning plus a distinct exit as the fallback if a refusal would break a legitimate caller shape. **It does not**, so the refusal landed:

- No caller constructs a body programmatically — every body is written by a seat, on stdin or in a file; nothing in the tree feeds this tool a quoted-only body.
- The remedy costs one token OUTSIDE the quotation, and both legitimate shapes the card names (the seat's own claim comments; the docblock shape) are accepted by the predicate.
- All three filed instances were repaired by hand afterwards, so the population wanted refusing, not warning.
- A warning on stderr is exactly what the false read-back line already was, and `EXIT_REFUSED` already means "the body broke the stamp contract, nothing written" — which is what this is.

Refusal ordering is unchanged (positional / mixed / quoted / unknown first); this rule is last, because it needs the counts.

## 3. The false status line, retired

`stamp: none substituted — this body carried no {{NOW}}, so there is no clock to check` was printed over three shapes and was true of one. The refusal closes the third before any write; `readBackVerdict` now reads the verdict for the other two and says what was quoted:

- `stamped-by-declaration` → names the declaration and, when openers were quoted, how many were left as text.
- `no-token` → the old sentence, now spelling "quoted or not" so it cannot be read as true of a quoted one.
- `unstamped-quoted-token` → unreachable through the CLI, and still true: it says the body DID carry a token and names the exit that refuses it.

The verdict also reaches the caller through the DRY RUN line and `--json` (`stamp_verdict`, `verbatim_tokens`).

## Measured after the change (same command shape, same fixtures)

| body | exit | reading |
|:---|:---|:---|
| LEG A — quoted-only | **2** | REFUSED, naming the opener (`` `{{NOW}}` ``), the construct (a backtick code span), the byte, and the missing stamp |
| LEG B — prose token | 0 | `stamped-by-this-act` — byte-identical substitution |
| `{{WAS:…}}`-only (the seat's claim shape) | 0 | `stamped-by-declaration` |
| docblock-shaped (quoted tokens + a declaration) | 0 | `stamped-by-declaration`, `verbatim: 2` |
| no token at all | 0 | `no-token` |

## Self-test

413 cases / 15 batteries → **477 cases / 16 batteries**. New battery, declared by name with its floor: `the stamp verdict: a quoted token is not a stamp, and the carve-out has a partner check` : 63. `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` 14 → 15; `the quoting spelling…` floor 51 → 52 (one case added there). Roster floors still sum to the case total.

Two existing fixtures were triaged rather than batch-edited:

- The one-line fixture ``Write `{{NOW}}` there.`` gained a prose `{{NOW}}`, so it still pins the carve-out while being a body that can be rendered.
- `QUOTED_WAS_DIGITS` is kept **byte-identical** and read through `substituteTokens` instead of `renderBody`: a quoted `{{WAS:…}}` with real digits and nothing else IS the refused shape now, so the three rendering cases are pinned on the walk that owns rendering and the acceptance decision is pinned where it is made. ⛔ Stamping that body with `{{NOW}}` is not the fix — the quoted digits are unmasked, so the MIXED refusal fires; that is pinned too.

## Reverse verification — two ablations, on-disk mutation proved, restore proved

Both through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit; blob hash before/after; restore asserted against `HEAD`), from a committed state, each predicted RED before running.

1. **The guard**: `if (verdict === REFUSED_STAMP_VERDICT) {` → `if (false && …) {`. anchor 1 → 0, blob `fbda5f0fbc99` → `1f6870303430`. ⇒ `✗ post-stamped self-test: 17 of 477 case(s) failed, 0 floor problem(s)` — LEG A, the three filed specimens and every refusal-text case go red. Restored: blob == HEAD `fbda5f0fbc99`, `git diff HEAD` empty.
2. **The read-back line**: `if (substituted === 0 && verdict === 'stamped-by-declaration') {` → `if (false && …) {`. anchor 1 → 0, blob `fbda5f0fbc99` → `707b4ca9747c`. ⇒ `✗ post-stamped self-test: 3 of 477 case(s) failed` — exactly the three false-line cases. Restored identically.

The first ablation originally aborted on a `TypeError` instead of listing failures; `df98cbf` reads those results through `String(...)` so each case reports itself, which is what an ablation has to be able to read.

## Gates

29 derived families (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, re-derived at the merged head `0e09e2b` — no STALE TREE warning), 29 run, exit codes captured before any pipe, all **0**. `pnpm check:pm-post-stamped` green. `--ran` reconciliation: `29 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 29 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.

The repo-wide scan was **not narrowed**: `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, 6,894 files in eslint's own population) ran whole and exited 0 at `0e09e2b`. Control-character self-scan over the changed file: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'` → no match.

`skip-changeset`: `scripts/pm/**` is in no package's `files[]` and publishes nothing.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed — none of these is a reproducible defect, a declared-contract violation or a metadata-authoring trap:

- `readBackVerdict`'s `unstamped-quoted-token` branch is unreachable through the CLI by construction (the refusal precedes the write). It is kept, and says the truth, because the function is exported and pure. Carrier for a future change: the next PR that gives this tool a second write path. Noted, not filed.
- The refusal's row prints a byte offset computed per opener with `Buffer.byteLength(text.slice(0, at))`. On a body with many quoted openers that is O(n·k); k is the number of quoted tokens in one artefact, so no real body reaches a cost worth a card. Carrier: none. Noted, not filed.

Serial: #19048 (exit-4 footer re-anchor) and #18995 (opening-line `{{WAS:…}}` / H56 parity) are not addressed here and remain open on this file.
